explanation:
## What the earlier attempts got wrong

The overall picture was right from the start. Red rays start at the red border cell. Each ray paints background cells red, and may pass over red it drew earlier. A ray that reaches the grid edge ends. A ray blocked by a coloured cell splits into the two perpendicular directions. That rule reproduces pairs 1 and 3 to 6 exactly. In pair 2 it also produces some branches the expected output does not have.

The second inspection listed every ray in the "always split" tree for pair 2. That listing rules out the "each obstacle deflects only once" idea. The expected output has red column 7, which can only come from the 7 at (1,8) deflecting row 1. It also has red cells (2,9)–(2,11) to the right, which can only come from that same 7 deflecting column 8. So that obstacle deflects twice, and the cause must lie elsewhere.

The extra cells in pair 2 trace back to two hits that should **not** split:
- the ray going left along row 1 from (1,4), which paints only (1,3) before the 8 at (1,2) blocks it;
- the ray going down column 4 from (9,4), which paints only (10,4) before the 7 at (11,4) blocks it.

Both of these rays move **only one cell** before being blocked. I checked this against every split the outputs require:

- **Pair 2:**
  - Column 2 moves 2 cells each way and splits.
  - Row 6 moves 6 cells, column 8 moves 4 and 3 cells, row 9 moves 4 cells, and column 4 upward moves 8 cells; all of these split.
  - Two more one-step rays must stay unsplit: column 5 upward ((1,5) only) and row 2 leftward from (2,8) ((2,7) only). That still fits the output, because the same red lines arrive from other branches: row 1 from column 4 hitting the 3 at (0,4), and column 7 from row 1 hitting the 7 at (1,8).
- **Pairs 3 to 6:** every splitting ray moves at least 2 cells.
- **Pair 1:** the only one-step split is the very first ray, (3,0) → (3,1), which is stopped by the 8 at (3,2).

**Rule:**
- A blocked ray splits perpendicular only if it moved at least 2 cells, or if it is the first ray leaving the red seed.
- Otherwise it simply stops.

I worked this through by hand for pair 2 only; the verifier will confirm it on all six pairs.

**On the test.** The red seed is at (3,0), so the first ray runs right along row 3 to (3,5) and is blocked by the 6 at (3,6). It splits up and down column 5, and every later ray follows the same "split only if it moved at least two cells" rule. The program emits a canvas for each ray that adds new red cells, then the final grid.

rays.text: Red rays start at the red border cell.
Each ray paints background cells red, and may pass over red it drew earlier.
A ray that reaches the grid edge ends.

validation: Frozen corpus recorded successful replay on teaching fixtures; synthetic generalization not established.
